{
  "analysis": "The training data reveals that German legal texts consistently identify persons through specific contextual anchors: judicial titles (Richter, Richterin) followed by academic/professional titles (Mag., Dr., Univ.-Prof.) and names, or parties in a case (Beschwerdeführer, Beklagte) often preceded by 'Herrn', 'Frau', or 'des'. The rules must leverage these strong context anchors to distinguish names from capitalized nouns.",
  "strategy": "Use three focused regex rules: one for judges/officials identified by title and role, one for parties identified by case role or direct address (Herr/Frau), and one for generic names appearing in lists or specific contexts like 'des [Name]'.",
  "note": "Every rule includes output_template and output_key. Patterns use lookbehinds/lookaheads to ensure context without consuming it, and capture groups to extract the name span accurately.",
  "rules": [
    {
      "name": "Judicial_Officials",
      "description": "Captures judges and officials identified by their role (Richter/Richterin) and professional titles (Mag., Dr., Univ.-Prof., etc.).",
      "format": "regex",
      "pattern": "(?<=die Richterin\\s+|durch den Richter\\s+|durch die Richterin\\s+)([A-Z][a-z]+(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)*(?:\\s+\\.[A-Z]\\.)?(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)*)+)",
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$1",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "person"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "priority": 10,
      "reasoning": "High precision anchor: 'Richter/Richterin' is a very strong indicator of a person in this domain. Captures the full name including titles like 'Mag.', 'Dr.', 'Univ.-Prof.'."
    },
    {
      "name": "Parties_Herr_Frau",
      "description": "Captures parties identified by honorifics 'Herrn' or 'Frau' followed by a name.",
      "format": "regex",
      "pattern": "(?<=Herrn\\s+|Frau\\s+)([A-Z][a-z]+(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)*)",
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$1",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "person"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "priority": 9,
      "reasoning": "'Herrn' and 'Frau' are strong context anchors for persons in legal texts. This handles cases like 'Herrn Domrose' or 'Frau Anton Frettlöh'."
    },
    {
      "name": "Case_Party_Genitive",
      "description": "Captures names in genitive constructions often used for parties, e.g., 'des [Name]' or 'der [Name]'.",
      "format": "regex",
      "pattern": "(?<=des\\s+|der\\s+)([A-Z][a-z]+(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)*)\\b(?=,|\\s|$)",
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$1",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "person"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "priority": 8,
      "reasoning": "Handles cases like 'des Alma Laurentzsch' or 'der Ruperta Rüdigkeit' where the name follows a genitive article. The lookahead ensures we stop at punctuation or end of string."
    },
    {
      "name": "Professional_Titles_Person",
      "description": "Captures names preceded by professional titles like 'KommR', 'RgR', 'StR', 'SV' which are common in legal texts.",
      "format": "regex",
      "pattern": "(?<=KommR\\s+|RgR\\s+|StR\\s+|SV\\s+)([A-Z][a-z]+(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)*)",
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$1",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "person"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "priority": 7,
      "reasoning": "Specific titles like 'KommR' (Kommissar), 'RgR' (Regierungsrat), 'StR' (Steuerberater) are strong indicators of a person's role and name."
    },
    {
      "name": "Name_List_Context",
      "description": "Captures names appearing in lists or specific phrases like 'für [Name]' or 'von [Name]'.",
      "format": "regex",
      "pattern": "(?<=für\\s+|von\\s+)([A-Z][a-z]+(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)*)\\b(?=,|\\s|$)",
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$1",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "person"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "priority": 6,
      "reasoning": "Handles cases like 'für Sibylle Wigandt' or 'von Selma Feldt'. The lookahead ensures we don't capture the next word if it's part of a compound noun."
    }
  ],
  "deleted_rules": []
}

{
  "analysis": "The training data reveals that German legal texts frequently use specific titles (Mag., Dr., Univ.-Prof., etc.) and role indicators (Richter, Richterin, Herr, Frau) to identify persons. The main challenge is distinguishing between full names, names with titles, and initials/abbreviations used as names (e.g., 'Dr. F', 'M.M.A.'). The rules must prioritize these contextual anchors to avoid matching common nouns or generic capitalized words.",
  "strategy": "Use a set of prioritized regex rules that anchor on specific legal titles, role indicators, and structural patterns (like 'Herr/Frau' followed by a name) to extract person entities, ensuring capture groups isolate the name portion for accurate span extraction.",
  "note": "Every rule includes output_template and output_key. Patterns use capture groups ($1) to extract the name while ignoring surrounding context like 'Herr' or 'Richter'.",
  "rules": [
    {
      "name": "Legal Titles with Full Names",
      "description": "Matches persons preceded by common German legal/academic titles (Mag., Dr., Univ.-Prof., etc.) followed by a full name.",
      "format": "regex",
      "pattern": "(?:Mag\\.|Mag\\.a|Dr\\.|Dr\\.in|Univ\\.-Prof\\.|Priv\\.-Doz\\.|RgR|StR|Ing\\.|Dipl\\.-Ing\\.|Dipl\\. Kfm\\.|MSc|Bakk\\. phil\\. B\\.|MedR|ÖkR|BA)\\s+([A-Z][a-z]+(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)+)",
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$1",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "person"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "priority": 10,
      "reasoning": "High precision rule for the most common pattern in legal texts: Title + First Name + Last Name. Captures the name part only."
    },
    {
      "name": "Herr/Frau Preceded Names",
      "description": "Matches persons preceded by 'Herr' or 'Frau' (often with titles like 'Herrn' or 'Frau' in different cases).",
      "format": "regex",
      "pattern": "(?:Herr|Frau|Herrn|Frau)\\s+([A-Z][a-z]+(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)+)",
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$1",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "person"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "priority": 9,
      "reasoning": "Covers cases where the title is a generic honorific rather than a specific academic/legal title."
    },
    {
      "name": "Role Indicators (Richter/Richterin)",
      "description": "Matches names following specific judicial roles like 'Richter', 'Richterin', 'Senat', or 'Schriftführer'.",
      "format": "regex",
      "pattern": "(?:durch\\s+(?:den|die)\\s+(?:Richter|Richterin)|in\\s+Anwesenheit\\s+der\\s+Schriftführerin|in\\s+Anwesenheit\\s+der\\s+Schriftführer)\\s+([A-Z][a-z]+(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)+)",
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$1",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "person"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "priority": 8,
      "reasoning": "Specifically targets the standard opening of legal decisions where the judge's name is listed."
    },
    {
      "name": "Initials as Names",
      "description": "Matches single letters or short initials used as names in legal contexts (e.g., 'Dr. F', 'M.M.A.', 'Hr Mag NN2').",
      "format": "regex",
      "pattern": "(?:[A-Z]\\.)?\\s*([A-Z]\\.[A-Z]\\.[A-Z]|[A-Z]\\.[A-Z]|[A-Z]\\s+[A-Z]\\.[A-Z]|[A-Z]\\s+[A-Z]\\s+[A-Z]|[A-Z]\\s+Mag\\.?\\s+[A-Z])",
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$1",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "person"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "priority": 7,
      "reasoning": "Handles anonymized or abbreviated names found in the training data which do not follow standard full-name patterns."
    },
    {
      "name": "Names in Parentheses/Context",
      "description": "Matches names appearing in specific contexts like '(Nachname wie Bf.)' or '(geboren am ...)' which often follow a name.",
      "format": "regex",
      "pattern": "(?:für\\s+die\\s+Tochter|für\\s+das\\s+Kind|Nachname\\s+wie\\s+Bf\\.?)\\s+([A-Z][a-z]+(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)+)",
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$1",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "person"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "priority": 6,
      "reasoning": "Captures family members mentioned in tax/family allowance contexts where the name might not have a preceding title."
    },
    {
      "name": "Representative/Attorney Context",
      "description": "Matches names following 'vertreten durch' (represented by) which often introduces a lawyer or representative.",
      "format": "regex",
      "pattern": "(?:vertreten\\s+durch)\\s+([A-Z][a-z]+(?:\\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)+)",
      "output_template": {
        "text": "$1",
        "start": "$start",
        "end": "$end",
        "type": "person"
      },
      "output_key": "entities",
      "priority": 5,
      "reasoning": "Identifies legal representatives who are persons but might not have the standard 'Mag.' or 'Dr.' title immediately before their name in all variations."
    }
  ],
  "deleted_rules": []
}

- GENERALIZE, DON'T MEMORIZE: Rules run on unseen text. Match the *structure* of values, not the exact strings you see in training data.
- USE CONTEXT: The same string can mean different things. Match surrounding words/punctuation and use capture groups ($1) to extract just the value.
- ONE RULE, ONE PATTERN: Multiple focused rules beat one giant regex. Each rule should have a clear, testable reason to exist.
- THINK ADVERSARIALLY: Before writing a rule, ask "what else could this match?" If the answer isn't empty, narrow the pattern or add context.

WHAT MAKES A GOOD RULE:
- PRECISION OVER RECALL: A rule that matches 10 things correctly beats one that matches 100 with 20 wrong. Never sacrifice precision for recall. Missing a match is fixable later; a wrong match poisons results.
- GENERALIZE, DON'T MEMORIZE: Rules run on unseen text. Match the *structure* of values, not the exact strings you see in training data.
- USE CONTEXT: The same string can mean different things. Match surrounding words/punctuation and use capture groups ($1) to extract just the value.
- ONE RULE, ONE PATTERN: Multiple focused rules beat one giant regex. Each rule should have a clear, testable reason to exist.
- THINK ADVERSARIALLY: Before writing a rule, ask "what else could this match?" If the answer isn't empty, narrow the pattern or add context.

- ONE RULE, ONE PATTERN: Multiple focused rules beat one giant regex. Each rule should have a clear, testable reason to exist.

- GENERALIZE, DON'T MEMORIZE: Rules run on unseen text. Match the *structure* of values, not the exact strings you see in training data.
